_comment: The content packs this viewer can offer to download.
A data file rather than a list in the code, so a pack can be added, its
size corrected or its URL moved without touching Python -- and so the set
of things a build offers is inspectable without reading a module.
Every field is required except 'companions' and 'family'.  'copyright' in
particular is mandatory and is checked by a test: the acknowledgements
screen is generated from these entries, so a pack that cannot state its
terms is a pack that would be redistributed unattributed.
'approximate_bytes' is what the user is shown before consenting and what
sets the fetch's size cap; measure it (an HTTP HEAD gives Content-Length)
rather than estimating, since a cap below the real size fails the download
'marker' is a path that proves the pack is already unpacked; empty means
the directory existing and being non-empty is proof enough.
There is deliberately no entry for Alien Arena's base art.  The only
source of it is its own game data, licensed for use solely within its own
engine, so this viewer may neither download it nor read an installed copy.
The symmetry with the Quake 3 entry is inviting and false.

packs.copyright: OpenArena project, CC BY-SA 3.0 / GPL; Debian main
packs.notes: Menu art, models, the ambient sounds, and -- the reason a viewer wants it -- the .shader scripts. Many surface names in these maps are shader names rather than file names, and resolve to nothing without them.

packs.copyright: Various authors, CC BY-SA 3.0 / GPL; Debian main
